links.outcome: Readability of ChatGPT-generated patient-facing notes versus original notes
links.effect: ChatGPT notes required higher reading proficiency than originals, with ChatGPT 3.5 demanding the most advanced level, despite expanding abbreviations.
links.quote: ChatGPT expanded abbreviations, but readability metrics showed that the notes required a higher reading proficiency, with ChatGPT 3.5 demanding the most advanced level.

links.outcome: Reading level of AI-generated patient notes relative to original notes
links.effect: Transformed notes required higher reading proficiency than the original; ChatGPT 3.5 required the most advanced level.
links.quote: ChatGPT expanded abbreviations, but readability metrics showed that the notes required a higher reading proficiency, with ChatGPT 3.5 demanding the most advanced level.

links.outcome: Medical fidelity of AI-generated patient notes, including omissions
links.effect: Medical fidelity ratings varied across three cases (GPT-4.0 rated superior); transformed notes omitted details impacting medical fidelity.
links.quote: While ChatGPT improved sentiment and empathy metrics in the transformed notes, compared to the original they also required higher reading proficiency and omitted details impacting medical fidelity.

screen.reason: Empirical evaluation of GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 rewriting clinical notes into patient-facing open notes on fictional vignettes, assessing readability, empathy, and medical fidelity without testing a specific organizational safeguard or deployment intervention.
